title: Kickoff SDK microflow templates and telemetry scratch
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working playbook for the first-run SDK experience (local dev -> sandbox -> first production call) focused on microflows and minimal telemetry requirements. Goal: give SEs and new hires 5–20 minute reproducible paths to ship simple integrations and exercise observability points.

Audience:
- Developer advocates and SEs running demos
- SDK maintainers making sure defaults are safe
- Integrators who need an express path to production proof-of-concept

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: flow templates, concrete commands, essential telemetry events/metrics, quick failure-mode tests, a minimal FAQ.
- Non-goal: full policy docs, exhaustive troubleshooting, or language-specific deep dives (those live in language-specific repos).

How to use this doc:
- Pick a microflow matching your use case (5-min quick hit or 30-min local-first loop).
- Run the smoke commands, check telemetry events in the sandbox project.
- If something fails, use the failure-mode checklist.

Microflow A — Zero-to-first-API-call (target: ~5 minutes)
- Purpose: confirm credentials, basic generation, streaming path.
- Steps:
  1) Create API key in Console (copy) or use existing sandbox key TEST-xxx.
  2) Minimal curl to confirm endpoint:
     curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-alpha-1\",\"input\":\"Say hi\"}'
  3) Expected: 200, body contains text field and token_count ~<50.
  4) If streaming required, use node example (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/examples/stream): node stream-demo.js --key $API_KEY
- Telemetry checkpoints to validate:
  - event.sdk_init (timestamp, lang, sdk_version)
  - event.request_sent (model, route, request_id, latency_ms_est)
  - metric.tokens_generated (count, model, customer_tier)

Microflow B — Local dev with stubbed runtime (target: 10–20 minutes)
- Purpose: iterate without external calls, deterministic samples, validation of client-side prompt logic.
- Steps:
  1) Clone lightweight stub server: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-stubs && cd sdk-stubs
  2) Start server: python -m http.server 8080 (or docker run -p 8080:8080 redwood/stub:latest)
  3) Point SDK to stub via REDWOOD_API_HOST=http://localhost:8080 and run quick unit flow: pytest tests/test_prompt_flow.py -k smoke
  4) Validate local telemetry capture: set SDK env REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_LOCALFILE=./telemetry.log and assert event lines appear.
- Notes: stub should return consistent sampling tokens to exercise caching behavior (prefix match).

Microflow C — Telemetry smoke + one-dashboard (target: 15 minutes)
- Purpose: verify telemetry ingestion and create a throwaway dashboard to show SLOs in demos.
- Steps:
  1) Deploy to sandbox account with API key and set REDWOOD_METRICS_EXPORTER=prometheus-scrape or OTLP endpoint.
  2) Generate 50 short requests with burst pattern (batches of 5, 10s pause). Use helper script: tools/telemetry-burst.sh --key $API_KEY --n 50
  3) In telemetry viewer (link: CONSOLE->Observability->My Sandbox) confirm:
     - requests/sec spike visible
     - 95th percentile latency < 400ms (for small model)
     - token distribution metric reports expected mean/histogram
  4) Save a dashboard snapshot for demo.
- Minimal telemetry fields to emit from SDK:
  - sdk.name (string), sdk.version (string), language (string)
  - request.id (uuid), request.model (string), request.tokens_in and request.tokens_out (ints)
  - request.latency_ms (int), request.cache_hit (bool), transport.error_code (string if any)

Microflow D — Failover and graceful degradation test (target: 20–30 minutes)
- Purpose: ensure client-level fallback to smaller model or cached result works.
- Steps:
  1) Configure two models in client config: primary=redwood-alpha-2, fallback=redwood-mini-quant
  2) Simulate primary failure: set REDWOOD_API_HOST to invalid host or kill network egress on sandbox VM
  3) Trigger 10 requests and confirm fallback path used (telemetry event request.fallback_used with fallback_model).
  4) Assertions to include in smoke script: no uncaught exceptions, user-facing error message <= 1 line, final response scored with fallback_model tag.
- Failure modes to document: partial responses, truncated streaming, non-idempotent retries.

Microflow E — Coldstart warmup ritual (target: 10 minutes)
- Purpose: reduce first-request latency by warming KV caches and kernels on Dedicated pools.
- Steps:
  1) Run warmup script: tools/warmup.sh --model redwood-alpha-2 --prefixes examples/warm_prefixes.txt --repeat 3
  2) Verify telemetry: metric.kernel_load_time drops after first wave, kv_cache_hit_rate increases.

Quick checklists (copyable):
- Pre-demo checklist (1–2 minutes):
  - [ ] Valid API key set in environment
  - [ ] SDK pinned to known-good commit
  - [ ] Telemetry flags enabled (to collect demo metrics)
  - [ ] Fallback model configured and tested locally

- Repo release checklist (for SDK owners):
  - [ ] Bump version in package manifest
  - [ ] Update changelog with clear migration notes
  - [ ] Smoke tests (Zero-to-first-API-call, Stub, Telemetry) pass on CI
  - [ ] Ensure default telemetry minimun fields are present

Observability / telemetry minimum contract (for SDK maintainers)
- Required events: sdk_init, request_sent, request_done, request_error, fallback_used
- Required metrics: requests_total, requests_failed, tokens_generated_total, latency_ms.p95
- Labels/tags: env (dev|staging|prod), org_id, model, sdk.language
- Privacy note: never capture full prompt text in telemetry; only store prompt fingerprints or hashes when necessary and documented.

Developer UX heuristics (short):
- First-run should be <5 min for a simple echo.
- Errors should be actionable: suggest likely root cause (bad key, network block, quota).
- Defaults must be conservative: low token cap, safe timeouts, automatic retry backoff.

Sample troubleshooting snippets (notes to self):
- If 401 right after key create: check origin policy, some sandbox keys are region-locked (CONSOLE->Key details).
- Streaming hangs on Windows: recommend using WSL or node 18+; add guidance in README.
- Telemetry missing events: verify REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT and ensure SDK uses background flush with at-least-once semantics.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should SDK surface a single telemetry opt-in var for demos vs full production? (tradeoff: privacy vs signal)
- Define a small set of example prefixes for warmup script that are representative across LLM tasks.
- Add a language-agnostic microflow that demonstrates function/tool-calls with a stubbed tool.

References and quick links:
- SDK examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/main/examples
- Telemetry design doc (confluence): CONFLUENCE-REDWOOD-TELEMETRY-12
- Relevant PR with telemetry fields: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep these microflows minimal and scriptable (shell + node + python).
- Add pre-built Docker image that bundles warmup prefixes and stub server for offline demos.
- Consider a tiny web UI for quickstart that runs the microflows behind the scenes and shows a dashboard snapshot.

-- end of scratch playbook --
